For one, two distinct, or three affinely independent base points, the vectors (1,z) are linearly independent, so linear functionals on the first tensor factor isolate each nonzero second factor.

For collinear z_i=z_*+t_i v, the independent vectors (1,z_*) and (0,v) give the two vector equations. A zero coefficient forces both remaining coefficients to vanish by eliminating one term with distinct t_i. Otherwise eliminate the first term to make the other two nonzero vectors proportional, then use the unweighted equation for the first.

Conversely a dependence of the three collinear augmented vectors gives a tensor dependence after dividing by the nonzero proportionality scalars. Evaluation at a common strictly negative argument makes all ratios positive.
